objective: Two independent components, one objective; they share no file and may be built in parallel. PART 1 (Russell turn boundary): Close two gaps docs/STEP-12B-BACKLOG.md recorded during the connected integration pass ("The proposal validator's unknown-field rule stops at the top level" and "`failProbe` still has no caller") and deferred only because an acceptance run was live. (1) `validateProposal` in server/services/russell/proposal.ts (~259) refuses a whole proposal for an unknown top-level field (KNOWN_FIELDS ~122, loop ~272) — the rule §24 states — but inside the `candidate` (~329-355), `probe` (~360-386) and `software` (~389-424) objects an unrecognised key is silently ignored, so §24's claim is broader than the code: a worker that believed an extra instruction nested in one of those objects would take effect has it dropped and the rest acted on. The turn manifest in server/services/russell/turn.ts already tells workers exactly `title`/`statement`/`duplicateOf` for a candidate (~420, ~500) and `title`/`objective`/`expectedOutcome` for software (~438), so compliant workers are unaffected. (2) `failProbe` (server/repos/russellProbes.ts ~293) has no caller: `runProbe` (server/services/russell/probe.ts ~169) catches network failures inside `fetchOnce`, but any other exception thrown after `startProbe` (for example a failed `permitLookup` or `recordObservation` write) escapes, leaves the probe RUNNING, and is resolved only when `listExpiredProbes` ends it at UNKNOWN on a later tick — so "the probe crashed" and "the probe ran out of time" are recorded identically and the candidate waits out the deadline. PART 2 (Build campaign row): Put the factory's two campaign readers that have routes and no browser caller on the Build screen. GET /api/factory/campaigns/:campaignId/pull-request (server/routes/factory.ts ~636-643, returns pullRequestFor's {title, body} from server/services/factory/pullRequest.ts ~182, or {title:null, body:null}) and GET /api/factory/campaigns/:campaignId/throughput (~626-633, returns ThroughputReport from server/services/factory/throughput.ts ~77, every number an EvidenceNumber {value, evidence, basis}). client/src/lib/factoryApi.ts (~311-314) has campaign() and briefing() only. CLAUDE.md §27 records that on the local plane the rendered pull-request body is the campaign's whole deliverable and 'the one person who has to act on it had nowhere to read what they were about to open'; client/src/russell/Build.tsx `CampaignRow` (~1045-1120) still says for a campaign with prRef and no prUrl that 'opening the pull request is a person's step' (~1100-1112) without showing the title or body. Add `FactoryApi.pullRequest(campaignId)` and `FactoryApi.throughput(campaignId)` (typing throughput with `import type { ThroughputReport }`). In CampaignRow add a 'Read the pull request it would open' disclosure, fetched only when opened, that renders the title and the body in a <pre> (or says plainly that none has been rendered when title is null), and a 'How fast it ran' disclosure, fetched only when opened, listing unitsPerHour, maxObservedConcurrency, concurrency.observed and concurrency.declared with each number's evidence class; a null value renders the words 'not measured' with its basis, never 0 or a dash.
expectedOutcome: PART 1: proposal.ts exports the allowed key sets for each part (candidate: title, statement, duplicateOf; probe: question, maxLookups; software: title, objective, expectedOutcome) and `validateProposal` refuses the whole proposal with a new refusal code `UNKNOWN_PART_FIELD` (added to the refusal union) when any of those objects carries a key outside its set, before anything else about that part is used; the refusal sentence names the part but not the offending key's value. probe.ts wraps the body of `runProbe` after `startProbe` so that an exception calls `failProbe` with a fixed explanation naming the failure category (the error's class name, never its message, since a message can carry row values) and returns `{ ok: false, reason: 'failed', outcome: null, lookups }` instead of throwing; a probe already COMPLETE is not overwritten (failProbe is guarded on PENDING/RUNNING). A FAILED probe is already picked up by the post-probe re-judgement (`probedAwaitingDecision` in server/services/russell/loop.ts reads state IN ('COMPLETE','FAILED')), so no loop change is needed. PART 2: Build's campaign rows can show the pull-request title/body and the throughput report on demand, using the existing routes, with UNKNOWN figures labelled as not measured.
nonGoals: Any migration, schema or policy change.
Any server route or service change
Changing ReleaseDecision, Submit, Repositories or allocation behaviour
Changing the probe envelope, the lookup budget, the verdict rules, listExpiredProbes or the loop.
Changing the turn manifest in server/services/russell/turn.ts, the action set, REQUIRED_PART, FIELD_LIMITS or any refusal that exists today.
Editing docs/STEP-12B-BACKLOG.md (it belongs to another objective's scope).
Fetching either reader before its disclosure is opened
Opening, publishing or merging a pull request from Brain
Recording an exception's message or stack in russell_probes.
Stripping unknown keys instead of refusing: the rule is refusal of the whole proposal.

acceptanceConditions.statement: PART 1: validateProposal refuses with UNKNOWN_PART_FIELD a CAPTURE_CANDIDATE proposal whose candidate carries an extra key (e.g. "projectId" or "priority" nested inside it), a proposal whose probe carries an extra key, and a REQUEST_SOFTWARE_CHANGE proposal whose software carries "repository"; each otherwise-identical proposal without the extra key validates exactly as before.

PART 1: Every key in each exported part key set appears as a quoted field name in server/services/russell/turn.ts's manifest instructions for the parts the manifest describes (candidate and software), asserted by reading that file, so the validator cannot refuse a key workers are told to send.

PART 1: When a step inside runProbe after startProbe throws (the test forces this by making the observation write reject), the probe row ends FAILED with completed_at set and an explanation that names the error class and does not contain the thrown message, and runProbe resolves rather than rejects.
PART 1: A probe that ran to completion is still COMPLETE with its verdict after the change, and calling runProbe again on a FAILED probe does not change it.
PART 1: tests/russellNervousSystem.test.ts, tests/russellRecovery.test.ts, tests/russellSoftwareJourney.test.ts and tests/intakeToResult.test.ts still pass and the repository typechecks.

PART 2: tests/buildPullRequestPreview.test.tsx: opening the pull-request disclosure on a campaign row requests /api/factory/campaigns/<id>/pull-request exactly once and renders the returned title and body text; no such request is made before it is opened.
PART 2: When the route returns {title:null, body:null} the disclosure says no pull request has been rendered and renders no empty <pre>.
PART 2: Opening the throughput disclosure renders each listed figure with its evidence class, and a figure whose value is null renders 'not measured' and its basis, never '0'.
PART 2: tests/buildRepositories.test.tsx and tests/factoryHttp.test.ts still pass and the repository typechecks.

rollbackRequirement: Revert the merge commit; no schema or data change.
